chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Fred Robbins and the Town Hall concert
summary: Robbins, enamored of Miguelito's showmanship, emceed and publicized the Town Hall concert that introduced Afro-Cuban jazz.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, a lot of things happened after that. All right, you and Miguelito Valdes were a guest on his show one time. There's a photograph of that, how did that come about?

Well, he was - he fell in love with Miguelito's showmanship. He went to La Conga many, many times and in account that I was the one to accompany Miguelito and already I was mentioned to be made the fusion between Afro-Cuban music and jazz that - Normally I was brewing, you know, to make a recording and to use us as a backing, Flip Phillips, Charlie Parker, Sonny Stitt and Dexter Gordon, all those guys, so he in order to start the publicity, to make the American public or the jazz-oriented people; so he invited Miguelito
and myself to go to his, as a matter of fact, we was there a few times.
Yes, we made a concert that he was the emcee.
Is that the concert at Town Hall where ....
.... where you formally introduced Afro-Cuban jazz?
Uh - Huh. Who else was on that bill that night, do you remember?
Ahh - mm mm - My band, just my band.
.... and Fred Robbins was the master of ceremonies?
He was the master of ceremonies and he was in charge of all the publicity because the tremendous audiences of ......
Did you get a lot of publicity for that jazz concert?
It was a success in account of publicity because it was practically how it started in American field. The jazz ....
